sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Effingham County
sections.html:
Responsibility is divided among four offices. Assessments are built and defended by the Supervisor of Assessments, disputes go to the Board of Review, and the Treasurer, acting as county collector, sends the bills and takes payment. Rates and post-sale redemption belong to the County Clerk.

  • Treasurer: 217-342-6844, County Office Building, 101 N. Fourth Street, Effingham, open weekdays from eight to four
  • Supervisor of Assessments: 217-342-6711, also the office to call when your mailing address for tax bills changes
  • Board of Review: meets on the fourth floor of the same building
  • County Clerk: 217-342-8433 for tax rates and levies, 217-342-6535 for redemption estimates

The county's online parcel search, reached through its property tax inquiry link, pulls up a bill by owner name or address. Have the ten-digit parcel number handy if you have it. It prints at the left side of the bill, under the owner's name.

sections.h2: Due dates and the billing cycle
sections.html:
Effingham County bills in two installments. For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, those were September 25 and November 6, and both are behind us. Dates are set each year when bills go out, so the stubs on your own bill are the final word.

Illinois collects a year behind, which the county calls a two-year cycle. Year one fixes each parcel's value as of January 1. Year two applies the rates, mails the bills and sends the proceeds to the taxing districts. The 2025 bills went out on August 21, 2026, and the Treasurer asks anyone who hasn't received one by September 11 to call. A missing bill is no excuse: the tax and any late penalty still apply.

The county collects for more than 90 taxing districts. It also bills drainage, mobile home and railroad taxes.

You can pay by mail, in person, at a bank or online. Bring or send the original bill, or one printed from the county website. Other paperwork carries a $1 copy fee.

  • By mail, with the installment stub and a check, postmarked no later than the due date
  • At the Treasurer's counter
  • At most banks in the county, but only while the bill is not yet late, because banks can't take past-due payments
  • Online by credit card or e-check, which adds a convenience fee and can take up to seven days to post

With an escrow account, your lender may want a copy of the bill, so ask. Once you've sold, and the closing statement leaves the tax to the buyer, pass any bill that reaches you along to the new owner.

sections.h2: Late payment and the tax sale
sections.html:
Delinquent tax picks up a 1.5% penalty each month, and the amount rises every 30 days. After the due date, only the Treasurer's office can take payment, by mail or online. For the 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the county's remaining steps run like this:

Effingham County delinquent tax steps, 2025 taxes payable in 2026
StepDateWhat happens
Certified delinquent noticesNovember 30, 2026Mailed with a $10 per parcel fee; no personal or business checks afterward
Online payment cutoffDecember 27, 2026Last day to pay by card or e-check
Tax saleJanuary 7, 2027Held in the North room of the County Office Building

The sale is of the unpaid tax, not of the house, and a payer can still settle up to one business day before it. The county has elected under Public Act 104-0553 to acquire all delinquent taxes as trustee for the taxing districts. After a sale, ask the County Clerk for a redemption estimate.

Your written complaint is due at the Board of Review 30 calendar days after the newspaper prints your township's assessment changes. Publication dates differ by township, so find the paper that covers yours. The Supervisor of Assessments hands out parcel-specific appeal forms at 217-342-6711 or assessor@effinghamcountyil.gov.

The Board hears testimony on property claimed to be over-assessed or under-assessed and either confirms the value or corrects it. Hearings wrap up in early February. Still unhappy afterward? Your next stops are the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board or circuit court.

Before you send anything in, get the Board's current rules and filing information. Keep a copy of every page you submit.

First-time exemption applications go to the Supervisor of Assessments' office, and renewal forms are mailed each February. The exemptions on the county's list are senior homestead and assessment freeze, annual lease agreement, home improvement, returning veteran (PTAX-341), disabled veteran (PTAX-342) and disabled person (PTAX-343). Dollar amounts come from state law and shift over time, so ask that office what applies now.

The Treasurer also helps senior citizens apply for the state real estate tax deferral and approves those who qualify.

An optional nine-month prepayment plan, called TREASURER 9, spreads next year's tax over monthly payments due on the 15th. It currently runs January through August, costs nothing and requires that you owe no delinquent taxes. Sign up by October 15. Payments follow the most recent tax amount for the parcel.

sections.h2: Effingham County housing at a glance
sections.html: Effingham County is in south central Illinois, anchored by the city of Effingham, its seat and biggest town, with Interstate 70 running through. Population is 34,519 with 15,520 housing units. Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $189,500, and homeowners live in 78.2% of the units. Median household income is $80,404 and median gross rent is $733.

How the tax is split is a negotiation between the two sides. The county tells anyone who bought in late 2025 or 2026 to check the closing papers or ask the closing agent whether tax is still owed, because the bill may have been addressed to the previous owner depending on recording dates.

If you're selling and the bill is unpaid, here is the order of work:

  • Pull the bill from the online parcel search or call the Treasurer.
  • Ask the collector's office for the exact balance, including penalty, so the title company can quote it.
  • If the parcel already went to a tax sale, ask the County Clerk for a redemption estimate.
  • Confirm the ten-digit parcel number on the contract matches the bill.
  • Pay the balance at closing from proceeds, or before the sale date if one is close.

A cash sale skips the lender's payoff process, but the tax still has to be settled with the collector before the title can clear.

faqs.q: When is the second installment of Effingham County property tax due?
faqs.a: For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the first installment was due September 25 and the second November 6. Bills go out in late summer and show exact dates on the stubs.

faqs.q: What does paying Effingham County taxes late cost?
faqs.a: Late tax costs 1.5% for each month, growing every 30 days. Once the due date passes, banks can't take the payment, so it goes to the Treasurer's office by mail, in person or online.

faqs.q: Does Effingham County sell my house if I don't pay property tax?
faqs.a: No. The tax sale is a sale of the unpaid tax, and the buyer charges interest on top. You can pay until one business day before the sale, or redeem afterward through the County Clerk.

faqs.q: Where does an Effingham County assessment appeal go?
faqs.a: To the Board of Review, within 30 calendar days after your township's assessment changes are published. Get the parcel-specific form from the Supervisor of Assessments at 217-342-6711.

faqs.q: Which Effingham County office explains my tax rate?
faqs.a: The County Clerk, at 217-342-8433, computes rates from each district's levy. The Supervisor of Assessments at 217-342-6711 covers assessed value and exemptions, and the Treasurer at 217-342-6844 handles bills and payments.
